subject: Biotechnology
title: In-Space Biomanufacturing
description: A micro-lesson that makes In-Space Biomanufacturing usable.

hook.text: Print organs in orbit — microgravity lets bioprinted tissues hold shape without scaffolds that collapse under gravity.

buildup.text: The ISS BioFabrication Facility prints cardiac tissue — cells organize naturally in microgravity without gravitational settling.

discovery.text: Fiber optics pulled in microgravity have fewer defects — ZBLAN glass fibers made in space outperform Earth-made counterparts.

twist.text: Returning products from orbit is expensive — only ultra-high-value biotech products justify the cost of space manufacturing.

climax.text: Axiom and Orbital Reef will dedicate station modules to biomanufacturing — orbital factories for pharma and biotech.

punchline.text: Make it in orbit, use it on Earth — space biomanufacturing creates what gravity prevents.

quiz.question: Why does bioprinting work better in microgravity?
options: Space radiation enhances cell growth and differentiation
Without gravity, printed tissues hold their shape and cells organize naturally instead of settling or collapsing
The vacuum of space sterilizes the bioprinted tissue automatically
